artists.name: Ivy Ross
artists.bio: Ivy Ross is devoted to a collaborative and creative vision of an emergent equitable world. She is a nationally recognized facilitator, musician, writer, and educator who addresses challenging social and environmental issues with compassion, critical thinking, playfulness, and flexibility, and she currently serves as the Director of Education for the Santa Fe Chamber Music Festival. She has served as consultant, facilitator, and performing artist for a multitude of organizations nationwide including: Children’s Defense Fund; Columbia Hospital For Women; Teachers & Writers Collaborative; Young Audiences; Children’s Cancer Association: MyMusicRX; the Anti-Defamation League, and The Boys & Girls Club. She is a certified Mindfulness Meditation Instructor, Hatha Yoga Teacher, Student Success Coach, and A World Of Difference Institute Trainer. Classroom teacher Emily Wahl says of Ivy, “She brings an attentive, gentle, cheerful, and patient attitude to teaching. It is clear that she finds inspiration in the responses of the children to the music, and gladly and adeptly incorporates their ideas. She is a joy to work with and the children respond with great affection and enjoyment to her sweet and fun style of teaching.”

artists.name: Heather Herd
artists.bio: Heather Herd is a classroom educator and teaching artist dedicated to student-centered learning, especially through movement, role-playing, and storytelling. She holds a B.A. in Dramatic Arts and Literature from Principia College and a Master’s Degree in Instruction and Curriculum from Kean University. Recognized for her creative approach to education, Heather was named a runner-up for the National Museum of Mathematics’ Rosenthal Award for Innovation in Math Teaching in 2015. She also designed a unit which is featured in the online course “21st Century Teaching and Learning” by Stanford Professor Jo Boaler, author of Limitless Mind and Mathematical Mindsets. Heather’s extensive background includes teaching K–8 across public, charter, and private schools in New Jersey and New Mexico—including Red River, Taos, and Santa Fe—as well as collaborating with the Lincoln Center Institute in New York City and Santa Fe's ALTO program. Heather thrives on sharing her creative energy in the classroom, helping students demonstrate understanding by bringing learning to life.

artists.name: Wendy Chapin
artists.bio: Wendy Chapin is a theater artist who began teaching in the Santa Fe public schools in 2001 independently as a theater teacher, working with integrated arts for the Alto Program, and working for Artworks a Lincoln Center Program sponsored by Partners in Education. She has taught theater arts to all ages from 7-70 for 40 years. Wendy is a theater artist who believes in collaborating with teachers to find ways to embody learning as well as creating opportunities for students to develop empathy as part of their interpersonal and intrapersonal experiences inherent when using drama in combination with curricular areas of study. Wendy has a BA in theater and history from the University of Colorado and an MA in Art Therapy from Southwestern College. She worked in professional theater on and off Broadway for 11 years.

artists.name: Liberty Yablon
artists.bio: Liberty Yablon is a sculptor, photographer and illustrator, born and raised in Santa Fe. She’s Also lived in Los Angeles where she worked in fashion design and film production. She loves to sew and design extravagant costumes. In downtime she crochets and loves time in nature. Before becoming a workshop leader with the Alto program, as well as ArtWorks, she taught art and theater full time for SFPS. She was an early member of art collective Meow Wolf and created immersive art experiences with them for 5 years. She’s passionate about teaching and loves working with students of all ages and backgrounds.

artists.name: Michelle Holdt
artists.bio: Michelle Holdt is an enthusiastic arts integration specialist and leader with a strong commitment to leading an arts rich life and making creative practice available for all children. She has over 20 years experience in arts education as a drama teacher, professional development leader, and arts administrator in a wide variety of educational settings. She was the Arts and Restorative Learning Coordinator at the San Mateo County Office of Ed and holds a Masters and Credential in Educational Administration from San Francisco State University, an Art Integration Certificate with The Alliance for Arts Learning Leadership, a BA in Drama and Human Development from Harvard University, a Masters in Theatre and Dance from the University of New Mexico, and a clear K-8 multiple subject credential from New College of California in San Francisco.

artists.name: Nancy Morris-Judd
artists.bio: Nancy Morris-Judd is an experienced teaching artist who has been delivering arts integration residencies to K-12 students since 2015. She collaborates closely with teachers to design residencies that align with specific curriculum goals and State Standards, customizing each project to fit the needs of both educators and students. Nancy is committed to providing practical arts integration tools that teachers can continue to use after the residency ends. A key goal is to inspire students to take an active role in their learning by offering creative opportunities for self-expression. Nancy also strives to meet the diverse needs of students by providing multiple ways for them to learn and demonstrate their knowledge. In addition to visual arts, Nancy’s residencies often include movement, theater, and music, creating an engaging and enjoyable learning experience for both students and teachers. Nancy has an Elementary Teaching Certificate but loves to work with students of all ages.

artists.name: Alejandro Jimenez
artists.bio: Alejandro Jimenez is a formerly-undocumented immigrant, poet, writer, and educator from Colima, Mexico, living in New Mexico. He placed 3rd at the 2022 Abya Yala Poetry Slam Championships held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, which brought together 15 national poetry slam champions from 15 countries in North, South, Central America and the Caribbean. He is the 2021 Mexican National Poetry Slam Champion, he is a two-time National Poetry Slam Semi-Finalist (US), multiple time TEDx Speaker/Performer, and a regional Emmy-nominated poet. In 2022, he was featured in TIME Magazine as one of 80 Mexican artists shaping contemporary Mexican culture. His work centers and touches on cultural identity, immigrant narratives, masculinity, memory, and the intersections of them all.

artists.name: Delia St. Louis
artists.bio: Delia St. Louis is an educator with a Master of Science in Education. She has classroom teaching experience dating back to 1999 in the New York City Public Schools and later starting in 2013 at Albuquerque Public Schools. She’s also the founder of Learning Without The Noise, a practice in which children learn tools and exercises that give them a unique advantage in learning and in life.

artists.name: Moira Garcia
artists.bio: Moira Garcia is a multimedia artist and bilingual educator. She is a New Mexico native and has worked in Santa Fe schools for over a decade. She holds a BFA in Studio Arts with a focus in Printmaking from the Institute of American Indian Arts, and a MA in Latin American Studies with concentrations in Art History and Indigenous Studies from the University of New Mexico. Her artwork is a visual language of symbol, color, and metaphor that often references and interprets ancient culture and cosmologies. As an educator, Moira is dedicated to meeting the needs of each student and guiding the expression of their unique and creative genius.

artists.name: Darryl Lorenzo Wellington
artists.bio: Darryl Lorenzo Wellington is the 2021-2023 Poet Laureate of Santa Fe, NM. He also writes a syndicated editorial column for The Progressive Media Project. Since 2016, he has been a Writing/Communications Fellow with Center for Community Change, a Washington DC-based organization that supports low-income people of color. Last year, he presented talks and workshops on poetry at over fifteen Santa Fe elementary, middle and high schools.

artists.name: Kathleen Kingsley
artists.bio: Kathleen Kingsley is a dancer/choreographer/dance educator. As co-founder of City in Motion Dance Theater in Kansas City, Missouri, she choreographed for and danced with the resident company, as well as working as an artist in education with Kansas City Young Audiences. She also initiated the first of four children’s dance theaters. She is a graduate of Anne Green Gilbert’s Summer Teacher Institute in creative dance. Her work in dance straddles both the teaching artist and school educator roles. As co-founder of the Río Gallinas School for Ecology and the Arts in Las Vegas, New Mexico she developed and taught the dance curriculum for grades 1-8. She established the dance department at the United World College of the American West (UWC-USA) and developed their International Baccalaureate Degree Program dance curriculum. She holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in Latin American studies. Currently Kathleen is co-founder and executive artistic director of MoveWest Center for Movement Exploration in Santa Fe and serves as ALTO’s residency program coordinator.

artists.name: Randy Barron
artists.bio:
Randy Barron brings over four decades of experience in arts and education. Since beginning his teaching career in 1980, he has worked extensively across the United States and abroad, including a 26-year tenure as a touring Kennedy Center Teaching Artist (1995–2021). He has led hundreds of professional development workshops for educators and teaching artists in forty U.S. states and in Singapore.
A professional dancer and choreographer, Randy performed with companies from Boston and New York City to the Midwest, and was a founding Artistic Director of City in Motion Dance Theater in Kansas City, Missouri. His leadership in the arts is matched by a wide-ranging commitment to education: he has served as a charter school founder, high school director, curriculum developer — and even a school bus driver.
Randy holds a Bachelor of Science in Biology and has also served his community as a volunteer firefighter and EMT. In recognition of his contributions to arts education, he received the Coll Award of Distinction from the New Mexico Art Education Association.

artists.name: Beth Ratay
artists.bio: Beth Ratay is a versatile composer who is able to craft music using a wide variety of styles and techniques. From music possessed of a quiet, understated grace, to music based on mathematical concepts, to emotive and hilarious opera, Ratay’s music is engaging, charming and beautiful. Dr. Ratay has had her music performed by diverse ensembles from across the United States. Her studies on the relationship of text to music in the work of Leoš Janáček and symmetric or layered musical structures in the music of Harrison Birtwistle strongly informs her own compositions. Beth also has been teaching music to people of all ages for over 25 years. Her experience includes individual instrumental and compositional instruction, music fundamentals and general education music courses for adults, and music basics for kids for all ages. Beth believes that learning music teaches many important and fundamental skills including social/emotional skills, math skills, and problem solving skills.

residencies.title: Breathing Life into Literature
residencies.description: Step into the spotlight and transform timeless myths, fables, and folklore from the page to the stage! In this hands-on, 8-session residency, 3rd through 5th graders will step into the shoes of both playwrights and performers. Students will unravel the core themes, character motivations, and structures of classic stories, then use dynamic drama techniques—like tableau, character voice work, and improvisational staging—to adapt them into original, short script performances. By weaving together reading comprehension, creative writing, and performance skills, young artists will discover how the stories of the past can find new life through their own unique voices.

residencies.title: Wind and Water Carve New Mexico: Dance the Story of Our Land
residencies.description: How did Ship Rock rise from the earth? What shaped the winding canyons of Tent Rocks? How did Glorieta Mesa come to stand so tall? In this lively, integrated dance-and-science residency, 4th and 5th graders choreograph living landscapes, stepping into the roles of wind, water and land and embodying the powerful forces that have shaped and continue to shape New Mexico. Working in collaborative groups, students transform the story of wind and water into original choreographed “living landscapes,” bringing geology to life through the elements of dance: body, energy, space and time. This process of turning words into movement, then movement phrases and then complete choreographies is carefully scaffolded for student success. Through creating choreography, students demonstrate science literacy, practice critical thinking, and build teamwork skills—while discovering that learning about New Mexico’s history can be as dynamic as the forces that shaped it.

residencies.title: Identity Investigation: An Exploration of Self and Community
residencies.description: In this residency, students will explore self and community using "arts based research." The residency begins with students building and constructing an "artful journal" with recycled materials and found paper ephemera. The journals then become a place to document their research on identity that ties to grade level appropriate NM social studies standards. Students will also experience a handful of scaffolded creative practices such as found word poetry, blind contour drawing, collage, and practice interviews that will support their arts based research. Students creatively record all of their key findings  in their journals, and in closing share them with each other in class.

residencies.title: Wonder Works
residencies.description:
In Wonder Works, students become question-detectives, using their bodies, voices, and imaginations to investigate the mysteries all around them — Why do we dream? What makes something fair? Where do
ideas come from? Instead of looking up answers, students step into them: freezing into human sculptures of an idea, interviewing a character who's never existed before, or turning a "what if" into a scene right before everyone's eyes.

Over the course of this residency, young performers won't just learn drama techniques — they'll learn to wonder on purpose. Every game, scene, and tableau is built to sharpen the skill that matters most in
school and in life: asking a great question and chasing it somewhere interesting. By the end, students won't just have answers. They'll have better questions — and the confidence to act on them.

residencies.title: Cosmic Calendars: Charting Sun, Moon, and Seasons
residencies.description: Students learn about celestial tracking of the sun, moon, and seasons, and the origins of the Western calendar as it relates to our solar system. With colored papers and mixed-media collage, students will create a giant calendar wheel of the four seasons and moon cycles while exploring the artist’s tools of color, geometry, and composition. Through classroom activities and the artistic practice, students will understand celestial patterns and develop a greater awareness of our relationship to the cosmos and how nature’s rhythms govern our experience of time. Artist educator Moira Garcia leads this exploration which aims to inspire wonder and creativity in the ways we observe and engage with the natural world and ourselves.

residencies.title: Creative Movement Skill-Building
residencies.description: Children love to move and learn through movement. But did you know that they also develop their brains through organized movement? Based on the dance elements of Body, Energy, Space and Time (BEST), BrainDance, and brain-compatible lessons plans, this 6-day residency serve as an introduction for Pre-K teachers and their classrooms to explore the possibilities within dance skill-building for classroom curriculum integration. Students build foundational movement skills through a blend of somatic awareness techniques and creative dance activities designed specifically for early learners. Kathleen encourages teachers to repeat activities between residency days, extending the learning and giving students the repetition young bodies and brains need to internalize new skills. Teachers walk away with strategies they can use long after the residency ends, and students build body awareness, focus, and coordination that support learning across every subject.

residencies.title: Look at That Flower!
residencies.description: Making realistic drawings can seem like a scary task to the average 4th-grader, and many assume that it is a matter of elusive talent rather than a skill process that they can learn. In this residency, students will learn to closely observe plants and insects native to Northern New Mexico and beyond. They will apply a variety of drawing techniques to create realistic illustrations of their choices of flora and fauna. As they work to finish their final product, they will also reflect on their process and create a written artist’s statement explaining the scientific discoveries and artistic choices they made along the way. They may discover that Artists and Scientists are really very similar.

residencies.title: ConteXt CodeX: Understanding Through Context
residencies.description:
Students often study events, texts, and ideas in isolation, missing the connections that make meaning clear. In this residency, students create accordion-fold codex books that help them explore how context—timelines, perspectives, related events—deepens understanding of any subject. Each codex features continuous pages for timelines and pockets for student-created inserts: maps, character analyses, thematic explorations, mini-zines, and personal reflections. Students organize and analyze information in ways that make sense to them, resulting in a personalized book that documents both their research and their thinking. By the end of the residency, every student completes a codex that demonstrates how understanding context helps us make sense of events, others, and ourselves more fully.

Planning Note: This residency works best when coordinated with an existing classroom unit. Students should have read a complete text or completed research on a topic before the first session. Nancy collaborates with teachers during planning to align the residency with curriculum goals while allowing students to choose specific topics within that frame.

residencies.title: Circles! In Art, Drama, Classroom, and Community
residencies.description: In this residency, students will explore circles as a theme in both visual art, drama, and community circles. Students will engage in a set of scaffolded creative practices such as found spiral drawings, simple mandalas, and playing drama games in a circle, and they will host community conversations and circles. Students will creatively record all of their sketches and artwork in their journals, and in closing share them with each other in class.

residencies.title: The Science of Sound
residencies.description: In this residency, students will explore various ways that sound can be created, and how to measure different lengths of a string, and how to determine the frequency or pitch of the string using sonic tools. Students will work together to find multiple pitches on a single musical string (monochord). When students actively determine how sound and pitch work, they will make important scientific connections, while exercising their measurement, data collection and data organization skills. After finding and measuring different pitches on the monochord, students will create a short piece of music using the newly discovered properties of the monochord. Dr. Ratay, musician, composer and educator, leads students on this journey of discovery and creation.

residencies.title: Mathematics Gets the Blues
residencies.description: Students will work together to write a blues song about mathematical concepts they have already learned in class by using the established lyric and musical pattern of that form. Along the way they will create and discover patterns and repetitions in groupings of 4, laying the foundations for addition and multiplication. By practicing these musical patterns within the metric framework, students will connect with these basic mathematical concepts in an entirely new way, cementing a greater, longer lasting understanding.

residencies.title: Cosmogram: Mapping a Cosmic Identity
residencies.description: Designed as a follow-up to Cosmic Calendars and for students with a primary foundation of astronomy and earth science. Using mixed-media and collage, students will translate their astronomical knowledge into a personal Cosmogram a.k.a. cosmic identity map. The Cosmogram will depict the phase and location of celestial bodies as well as the season and geography of the student's time of birth. Students will learn how to access and interpret the astronomy of their birth time and track the current moment. Guided by artist and astro enthusiast Moira Garcia, this residency will fortify and expand previous knowledge and cultivate a deeper relationship to the cosmos and personal identity.

residencies.title: The Passion Project, An Exploration of Self and Identity
residencies.description: In this residency, students will explore a self-selected topic connected to their personal identity using "experiential arts based research." The residency begins with students building and constructing an "artful journal" with recycled materials and found paper ephemera. The journals then become a place to document their research on identity that ties to grade level appropriate NM ELA standards. Students will participate in a handful of scaffolded creative practices such as found word poetry, blind contour drawing, and practice interviews as they begin their research. The students will then research on their own using “non-screen based” modes of learning including but not limited to: interviewing experts, having an experience, reading a book, observational drawings, and MORE! All of their key takeaways are creatively recorded in their journals and shared with each other on the final day of class.

residencies.title: Shapes in Motion: Exploring 2D and 3D Worlds
residencies.description: Step into the realm of geometry where shapes step off the page and onto the stage! In this energetic, 3-session residency, 2nd graders will combine math and creative drama to bring two-dimensional plane shapes and three-dimensional solids to life. Through playful physical tableau, body-sculpting, and movement exercises, students will explore vertices, edges, faces, and spatial relationships. By transforming abstract geometric concepts into interactive stories and dynamic living sculptures, young mathematicians and performers will discover how math shapes the world around them—and how they can use their own bodies to construct it!

residencies.title: Cosmic Calendars: Charting Sun, Moon, and Seasons (Abbreviated)
residencies.description: This shorter residency focuses on tracking time through understanding the lunar phases OR the four seasons. Students will work in groups to create a collaborative collage of the moon cycles and solar system OR a calendar wheel of the four seasons while exploring the artist’s tools of color, pattern, geometry, and composition.

residencies.title: Math on the Move
residencies.description: Many students feel frustrated when asked to master math skills without understanding the underlying concepts or how those skills connect to real life. This dynamic residency helps students explore numeracy, symbols, and geometry through collaborative choreography and creative movement. Using dance to represent mathematical ideas, students develop both individual and small-group movement studies that highlight the simple but powerful principles behind everyday math. Along the way, they engage in evaluation, editing, and revision—strengthening both their mathematical thinking and artistic expression.

residencies.title: Poetry as the Means We Need: Spoken Word & Performance Poetry
residencies.description: Seen as a “step-child” of academic poetry, spoken-word/performance poetry (or slam poetry) is a poetry form that is infinite and accessible to all students. This type of poetry, most importantly, opens the door for poets to use their whole body, and space, to make a poem come alive! In this workshop, through different writing exercises, students will write their own spoken-word poems and will be exposed to different performing styles and will learn memorizing techniques to recite their poem like a seasoned poetry slam poet. This workshop will ask students to explore the power of their own story as a means to create change, not be forgotten, and inspire others to do the same.

residencies.title: Rock Cycle: Story of Sand
residencies.description: Rocks don't just sit there — they travel, break, and transform through processes of nature. In this integrated science/dance residency your students are invited to become that process by  embodying the sequence that breaks down rocks to sand, and the roles that water and wind play in that process. We look at various New Mexico locations where that process is clearly visible. The dance content is based on these naturally occurring events, and invites students to improvise and build dance phrases that embody these  important geological events. Working collaboratively in small groups, students translate what they've observed into movement, creatively sequencing their own dance "text" that tells the story of sand from rock to grain and  transforming abstract science concepts into something they can see, feel, and share. The result: a science concept that usually lives on a worksheet becomes something students have physically experienced and can explain in their own words — and bodies.

residencies.title: Exploring History through Songwriting
residencies.description:
Turn what your students are already learning into music they'll never forget. Whether it's a unit on New Mexican history, or any other topic your class has been exploring, this residency transforms that existing knowledge into an original corrido (ballad).

When students create a piece of music about a subject they're already studying, they greatly increase their comprehension of that content and gain important learning skills. In this residency, students will work together to create a corrido based on material from their current classroom studies whether a historical figure or event, a book they've read, or another subject their teacher identifies. Dr. Beth Ratay, an experienced composer and scholar of world musics, leads this session, guiding students to synthesize what they already know, drawing on notes, journals, discussions and other types of class work, into a deeper, more personal understanding of the material through the art of storytelling in song.

residencies.title: Inner Compass
residencies.description: Students often struggle with stresses that make it difficult for them to engage with learning in the classroom; practicing a creative process can help them find ease and calm within themselves, so they can focus on their studies. In this 5-session residency, students learn how to embody the practice of “Learning without the Noise.”  That “noise” can be other students’ behaviors, transitions from one activity to another, negative self-talk, frustration, or comparing self to others. Through movement, vocal expressions, art and daily rituals, students will develop an awareness of how capable they can be with managing their inner and outer environment.

residencies.title: PE with the Brain in Mind
residencies.description: "Movement is the architect of the brain," says renowned dance educator Anne Green Gilbert — and this residency brings that principle directly into your PE space. Built on Gilbert's proven lesson plan format and based on the dance elements of Body, Energy, Space and Time, this residency introduces and equips PE teachers with developmentally appropriate strategies to strengthen fundamental movement skills in early elementary students. Beyond motor skills, students build cooperative group work and self-awareness through creative movement activities — skills that transfer well beyond the gym. And because lessons are aligned with New Mexico Physical Education standards for targeted grade levels, this residency fits directly into what you're already required to teach, not alongside it. All children love and need to move, and they delight in organized movement.

residencies.title: Poetry as Narrative Writing
residencies.description: This engaging residency supports narrative writing standards by helping students craft compelling stories using poetic forms and conventions. Students learn to identify main ideas, develop coherent sequencing, and express their voices through structured yet creative writing. By blending elements of poetry and narrative, students explore both fictional and non-fictional storytelling, discovering how imagery, tone, and structure can deepen the impact of their narratives. The residency fosters inquiry, creativity, and reflection, while reinforcing essential writing skills such as organization, clarity, and revision.

residencies.title: Be Your Own Poet Laureate
residencies.description: This five-session residency supports key writing standards by guiding students through reading, analysis, and the creation of original poetry. Students engage in close reading of diverse poems, develop critical thinking through discussion and peer critique, and build fluency in writing through multiple drafts of their own work. As they explore questions like “What makes something a poem?” and “Why does a metaphor work?”, students deepen their understanding of figurative language, voice, tone, and structure. They also practice revision and reflection—essential components of the writing process.

residencies.title: Act it Out! – Words Come Alive in Theater
residencies.description:
Students get on their feet and explore how words work in this literacy residency for 3rd and 4th graders, using theater as the learning vehicle. In Sessions 1–3, students build foundational acting skills — body, voice, imagination — through ensemble-building theater games. In Sessions 4–6, they apply those skills to create original skits that bring morphemes to life, strengthening vocabulary and word-analysis skills while building confidence and collaboration.
For their final product, small groups perform skits dramatizing the meaning of an assigned prefixed word (e.g., rewrite, dishonest). Students then "break character" to teach the audience how to break the word into its prefix and base, and explain how the prefix changes the meaning of the word — turning word study into a public-teaching moment for the whole class.

residencies.title: Embodying Biography: Walking in Another Person's Shoes
residencies.description: Step across time and step into the shoes of the changemakers, innovators, and leaders who shaped our world! In this dynamic, 8-session residency, 3rd through 6th graders will bridge social studies research with performance art by turning historical facts into powerful theater. Building on their own research of notable historical figures, students will master the art of monologue writing—exploring point of view, subtext, and historical context. Through voice training, physical characterization, and dramatic pacing, young historians and actors will transform textbook facts into compelling first-person performances that bring history vividly to life on stage.

residencies.title: Gelli Printing, Pop-Ups, & Accordion Books
residencies.description:
Do your students struggle to engage with classroom curriculum? In this hands-on residency students will learn how to Gelli print and build their own visual journals and pop-up accordion books. Using acrylic paints and Gelli Plates and different book building strategies, students will learn to make a book that will truly become their own. Those books will hold notes from class discussions, scribbles, poetry, collage, drawings, and MORE! 

At the end of the residency, the class will share their journals and art work with a gallery walk and each student's highly individualized self-exploration & expression.

residencies.title: El Agua es Vida: A Dive into New Mexico History
residencies.description:
What is an acequia? What is its cultural and practical importance to New Mexicans? In this integrated dance, history, and cultural studies residency, students dive into the history of place through the lens of water in New Mexico: ancient Indigenous methods of water collection and irrigation, the Spanish introduction of the acequia system with its defined roles and hierarchy, and the different perspective brought by American settlers. Working in small collaborative groups, students become "water historians." Using specially designed "expert packets," they read, discuss, and mine primary-source ideas to build original choreography — turning research into movement and history into something felt. Along the way, students strengthen reading-for-information, synthesis, and verbal communication skills, while experiencing firsthand how history, culture, and science can flow together and be expressed in movement through a process that is creative, memorable, and meaningful.

This residency is best fit for students with some grounding in reading for information, synthesizing ideas, and working effectively in groups — students are asked them to think, discuss, and move collaboratively.

residencies.title: Meaningful Symbolism: Petroglyphs to Pop Culture
residencies.description: In this hands-on residency students learn to communicate visually through engagement with ancient petroglyphs from local historical sites. They explore a bit of New Mexico history and think critically about historical and modern forms of communication, storytelling and persuasive cultural engagement. They develop an artistic lens to bring their knowledge of historical and modern symbolic expression to life.

residencies.title: Arroyo Songs! — Songwriting meets Science
residencies.description: Aligned closely with state and district standards, this hands-on residency integrates science, literacy, and the arts to meet educational objectives in an engaging and interdisciplinary way. In this residency, students write a song from the perspective of plants or animals in the arroyo. Students engage in a collaborative creative process that encourages critical thinking and synthesis of knowledge, transforming scientific ideas into expressive, memorable songs that they then record and share.

residencies.title: Frozen in Time: Dramatizing History
residencies.description: Step inside the moments that defined our world! In this immersive 8-session residency, 3rd through 5th graders will blend social studies research and physical theater to transform pivotal historical events into dynamic "living statues"—or tableaus. Working either across distinct historic milestones or deep within key moments of a single event, students will analyze historical perspective, spatial tension, and emotional impact to build frozen dramatic scenes. Paired with original student-written narration, these living snapshots will give voice to the figures of the past, turning static textbook timelines into vivid, multidimensional history brought to life on stage.

residencies.title: Finding the Math in Musical Patterns
residencies.description: By identifying and creating musical patterns, students connect with basic mathematical concepts in an entirely new way, cementing a greater, longer lasting understanding of patterns and how they shape our world. Students will identify patterns in familiar songs and create and share simple patterns using musical instruments and body percussion. Dr. Ratay guides students through this creative process, while demonstrating how mathematics and music intertwine to create patterns pleasing to the mind and the ear alike.

residencies.title: The Music of Math
residencies.description: In this residency, students will explore how the site or length of an instrument changes the pitch or frequency of a sound, and learn about how to work with fractions by using pre-measured monochords (a one string instrument) to get hands on, practical experience with counting and using fractions. When students make auditory connections with how fractions work, they make mental connections in a way that is outside typical math learning experiences. Throughout this process students will improvise and compose a short pieces of music using the newly discovered properties of the monochord and other instruments. Dr. Ratay, musician, composer and educator, leads students on this journey of discovery and creation.

residencies.title: The Garden of the Three Sisters
residencies.description: Students discover the traditional crops of corn, beans, and squash—and how they work together to enrich soil, protect one another, and thrive as a community. Alongside planting and sprouting demonstrations, students connect farming practices to New Mexico history and global traditions of sustainable growing. Younger grades explore through costumes and play, while older students focus on science concepts such as life cycles, soil health, and cross-pollination. Hands-on activities encourage observation, problem-solving, and creativity and help students develop transferable skills across the curriculum.

residencies.title: The Story of the Valles Caldera: Dancing the Forces That Shape the Earth
residencies.description:
What happened in the Valles Caldera? What if your students could be a volcano? In this high-energy, dance-integrated science residency, learners step inside the drama of one of the Southwest’s largest geologic wonders: the Valles Caldera.
Armed with “expert packets” of engaging, leveled content, small groups investigate the science behind volcanic formation and plate tectonics—convergence, divergence, subduction, translation, and uplift—then bring those forces to life through original choreography. As students embody shifting plates, building pressure, and explosive eruptions, they strengthen their science  vocabulary, reading-for-information skills, synthesis, and teamwork. Their finished choreographies presented in order trace the chain of events leading to the Valles Caldera’s cataclysmic eruption and its volcanic aftermath, making earth science unforgettable, tangible, and full of movement.

residencies.title: Water Dances: Dance Meets Science
residencies.description: In this dynamic, integrated dance-and-science residency inspired by Thomas Locker’s *Water Dance*, students don’t just learn about water—they *become* it. Working in small, collaborative groups, they transform text, imagery, and video into living, moving waterscapes. From the first trickles high in the mountains to roaring rivers and rolling oceans, students embody the power of water as it shapes our planet.Through a series of creative “dance challenges,” learners experiment, problem-solve, and choreograph original movement sequences that capture the rhythms, patterns, and forces of water. Along the way, they deepen their understanding of earth science while building teamwork, communication, and performance skills. With a carefully scaffolded progression, every student experiences success, pride, and the thrill of bringing science to life through art.

residencies.title: Dancing New Mexico's Stories: Poetry in Motion
residencies.description: What if your students could feel a poem, not just read it?  In this residency, poetry becomes a springboard into movement, encouraging students to connect more deeply by embodying and expressing the emotion and meaning behind the poem.  Working in small collaborative groups, students take on "choreography challenges," starting with simple words and phrases, and building toward transforming a whole poem into a dance "text" that captures its imagery and emotional core. Younger students might dance simple haikus, while older students dig into the rich, complex language of New Mexican poets like Levi Romero, Jimmy Santiago Baca, Nora Naranjo Morse, and Michelle Otero. Along the way, students build literacy skills, collaboration, and confidence — while discovering that comprehension isn't just something that happens in your head.
